sources.title: GitHub - RajatDandekar/SmolVLA_MRL2Bootcamp
sources.snippet: A complete pipeline for teaching a SO-101 robot arm to pick up a box and place it in the correct colored bowl using SmolVLA (Vision-Language-Action model) with natural language instructions. The robot understands not just "blue bowl" but also "the bowl that looks like the ocean" — semantic grounding from SmolVLA's VLM backbone.

sources.title: Fine-tuning SmolVLA for Cube Pick-and-Place on SO-101
sources.snippet: I decided to go with SmolVLA from HuggingFace, as it's a compact VLA built on SmolVLM that you can fine-tune on consumer hardware (in my case, RTX 3090). The idea is simple: collect teleoperation demos, fine-tune the pretrained model, and deploy.

sources.title: Train an SO-101 Robot From Sim-to-Real With NVIDIA Isaac
sources.snippet: You'll train and deploy a vision-language-action (VLA) model to perform unstructured pick-and-place of centrifuge vials into a rack using an SO-101 robot arm - first in sim, where we can iterate quickly and validate behavior, then in reality.
